one_line: Admins can schedule a date and time for an upcoming play session, which is shown on the BYOND hub status line so players know when the server will next be active.
player_facing_mechanics: See the scheduled play session date/time rendered in the server status (BYOND hub) text
Open a link to view the scheduled time converted to the viewer's local timezone
Admins can open a date-picker UI to set the playtime (no direct player action otherwise)
tg_systems_used: custom frogui UI framework (SSfrogui) with an HTML datepicker
data_only_parts: ADMIN_VERB metadata for schedule_playtime (category R_FUN, ADMIN_CATEGORY_SERVER)
The datepicker.html form asset selecting a datetime string
logic_parts: Parsing the ISO-like datetime string (year/month/day/hour/min) and computing weekday via iso_to_weekday/day_of_month
Building the AM/PM hour conversion and player-facing status string (with localtime link)
Updating the world/hub status after the admin confirms the date
byond_specific: world proc override (/world/proc/add_playdate) and world.update_status() hub status text
BYOND text procs: text2num, copytext, iso_to_weekday, day_of_month
ADMIN_VERB macro system and admin verb datums
HTML hyperlink embedded in status text pointing at external https://forgman6.github.io/?isoString=... service
SSfrogui.open_ui/close_ui with HTML file2text and topic (href_list) handling
port_notes: SS14 has no direct equivalent of BYOND's hub status text, so the core value (advertising a next-session time on the server browser) must be re-thought rather than ported one-to-one. A port would add a small server-side component/system holding the scheduled DateTime plus an admin command or console-accessible setter, and surface it via lobby/round-end UI, chat announcements, or Discord/gateway instead of hub status. The admin workflow maps to an admin command with a TGUI DateSelector/dialog rather than a frogui HTML form. Design questions: whether 'scheduled playtime' is meaningful in SS14's server listing, where the time should be displayed to players, and whether the external local-time link (forgman6.github.io) is acceptable to depend on.
